correctness.rationale: Bezout proves Q(s)=Q(theta); the irreducible minimal polynomial divides \(X^A-X^B-c\) with nonzero rational \(c\). A derivative sign table covers all coprime parities and proves at most three real roots; three roots enforce the strict rational-gap inequalities. The degree/signature parity identity gives the upper bounds. The reciprocal Eisenstein polynomial \(eX^d+3X^{d-1}-3\) proves irreducibility of both explicit witness families, and exact sign intervals establish 2, 3, or 1 distinct real conjugates for each degree. A fresh exact checker confirms finite examples; infinite correctness is proof-based.

value.rationale: A just-published problem classifies simultaneous rational powers for quadratic radicals. The natural arbitrary-degree variant has a complete, sharp number-field signature spectrum, explicit witnesses with positive shifts and negative bases for every degree, and a strict no-simultaneous-integer-output obstruction for the three-real-place branch. This is a motivated structural classification, not a computational slice; it does not purport to classify individual fields or all exponents.
